# A section-balanced circuit with no favorable Minkowski direction

This exact calculation concerns an auxiliary one-fiber statement. It does
not make the chosen point a mixed-integer deepest center, and it does not
make the individual sections centroidal there. Those additional conditions
must not be silently inferred from the circuit balance below.

Let K be a d-simplex, d>=2, with barycentric coordinates lambda_i,
i=0,...,d. Let x_0 be an interior point and put a_i=lambda_i(x_0),
t_i=1-a_i. Thus 0<t_i<1 and sum_i t_i=d. Use the d+1 central caps

    H_i={lambda_i>=a_i}.

Let F_i be the facet lambda_i=0, of area A_i, and let u_i be the unit
normal of H_i. The cap section area is S_i=A_i t_i^(d-1). The divergence
formula for the simplex gives sum_i A_i u_i=0 (the u_i are negatives of
the outward facet normals). Thus the positive circuit weights rho_i are
proportional to A_i, and the section-balanced probabilities are

    theta_i = t_i^(1-d)/Z,    Z=sum_i t_i^(1-d).

Indeed sum_i theta_i S_i u_i=0. On a body facet F_j, cap i is empty if
i=j and occupies the fraction t_i^(d-1) of F_j if i!=j. Consequently

    sum_i theta_i |F_j intersect H_i| = (d/Z) A_j             (1)

for EVERY body facet j.

Take any compact convex Minkowski summand L, and deform K to K+tL for
t>=0, holding the cap halfspaces fixed. The first-order body boundary
speed on F_j is its support value h_L(n_j). The usual swept-facet
calculation gives

    D|K+tL| = sum_j A_j h_L(n_j),
    sum_i theta_i D|(K+tL) intersect H_i|
      =sum_j h_L(n_j)sum_i theta_i |F_j intersect H_i|.

New pieces near lower-dimensional faces contribute o(t); all the cap
sections here are proper and their intersections with body facets have
zero facet measure. Substituting (1) proves the exact identity

    sum_i theta_i D|(K+tL) intersect H_i| = (d/Z) D|K+tL|.    (2)

It holds for every L, not merely homothetic or symmetric summands. If
0 belongs to L, these are feasible outward Minkowski directions and the
body-mass derivative is nonnegative. Whenever it is positive, the ratio
in (2) is exactly d/Z, independent of L.

Convexity of t^(1-d) and sum t_i=d give

    Z >= (d+1)(d/(d+1))^(1-d),
    d/Z <= (d/(d+1))^d=gamma_d.

Strict inequality holds unless all a_i=1/(d+1), and the ratio tends to
zero as one a_i tends to one. Thus interiority and the section-weighted
positive circuit balance alone cannot guarantee a Minkowski direction
with normalized own-circuit derivative at least gamma_d.

An entirely rational planar instance is the standard triangle with
a=(1/2,1/4,1/4), t=(1/2,3/4,3/4), and theta=(3/7,2/7,2/7).
Each edge's weighted trace fraction is 3/7, strictly below gamma_2=4/9,
with gap 1/63. Explicitly the three edge fractions are

    (2/7)(3/4)+(2/7)(3/4)=3/7,
    (3/7)(1/2)+(2/7)(3/4)=3/7,
    (3/7)(1/2)+(2/7)(3/4)=3/7.

At this point the facet-parallel sections are not all centered at x_0.
The statement requiring individual stationary-section centroids is
therefore a different, stronger auxiliary statement and is not refuted.
